 Sub: Annual Report of the Company for the Financial Year 2025-26 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
  
The 17th Annual General Meeting  (‘AGM’) of Inox Wind Limited  (the ‘Company’) is scheduled 
to be held on Friday, 25th September, 2026 at 3.00 P.M. (IST) through Video Conferencing/ 
Other Audio-Visual Means (‘VC/OAVM’).  
 
Pursuant to Regulation 34 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, please find enclosed herewith the copy of the Annual Report for the Financial Year 2025-26, inter-
alia, containing the Notice of the AGM. The same is also available on the Company’s website at 
https://inoxwind.com  and is being dispatched today to all the eligible shareholders whose e-mail Ids 
are registered with the Company/ Depositories. Further, a physical letter providing the web-link, 
including the exact path, where complete details of the Annual Report is available, have been sent to 
those shareholder(s) whose e-mail ids were not registered. 
       
The Company is providing to its Members the facility to exercise their right to vote on the resolutions 
proposed to be passed at the AGM by electronic means. Only a person whose name is recorded in the 
Register of Members or in the Register of Beneficial Owners maintained by the Depositories as on the 
Cut-off date i.e., Friday, 18th September, 2026 , shall be entitled to avail the e-Voting facility.  
 
The remote e-Voting facility commences on Tuesday, 22nd September, 2026 from 9.00 A.M. 
(IST) and will end on Thursday, 24th September, 2026 at 5.00 P.M. (IST) .  
 
We request you to kindly take the same on record.   
 
Thanking You  
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Inox Wind Limited

About INOXGFL Group
Transforming India’s Energy Horizon, 
Scaling New Heights
INOXGFL Group has emerged as a diversified Indian 
conglomerate with businesses across specialty 
chemicals and renewable energy, with its legacy and 
expertise spanning over nine decades. 
Through its listed entities and integrated 
business ecosystem, the Group operates 
across fluorochemicals, battery materials, 
renewable power solutions, clean 
energy infrastructure, renewable power 
generation and solar cell and module 
manufacturing, bolstering India's industrial 
and energy transition.

About INOX Wind
Accelerating India’s Energy 
Transition, Building Momentum
We are one of India’s leading integrated wind energy solutions providers, 
delivering end-to-end capabilities across the wind power value chain. Our 
offerings encompass wind turbine manufacturing, renewable infrastructure 
development (wind, solar, BESS), EPC, and O&M, thereby, supporting our 
customers throughout the lifecycle of a renewable energy project.
We are one of the most integrated players in India in the energy transition space. INOX Wind’s integrated business model includes 
manufacturing, project development, EPC, and O&M to deliver end-to-end renewable energy solutions (including wind, solar, BESS). 
Each stage of the value chain optimises operational synergies and project delivery and support enduring and sustainable value for our 
customers through a seamless and scalable business ecosystem.
Accomplish market leadership in the wind 
turbine Original Equipment Manufacturer 
(OEM) arena through technical expertise 
and operational excellence.Establish ourselves as the leading provider of integrated wind energy solutions 
domestically and expand globally, maintaining alignments with values of all our 
stakeholders and the evolving market dynamics and their emerging requirements.
This is being attained by:
 Expansion of our manufacturing facilities.
 Establishment of a product suite that provides customers with diverse options 
of competitive energy solutions.
 Enhancement of quality focus and identifying it as a key business pillar.
 Augmentation of wind farm sites’ inventories and bolstering of project 
management capabilities.
 Consolidation of market position in India and globally. Performance and excellence
 Cost-effective solutions
 Reliability and integrity
 Diversity and inclusionWe manufacture wind turbine 
generators and key components 
designed for diverse wind regimes, 
backed by a continuously evolving, and 
value-compounding product portfolio, 
consisting of 2 MW, 3 MW and the 
upcoming next-generation 4.X MW 
turbine platforms manufactured across 
our 4 state-of-the-art facilities in Gujarat, 
Himachal Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.Our services include turnkey EPC 
solutions spanning project development, 
engineering, procurement, construction, 
installation, commissioning and grid 
connectivity, pure equipment supply and 
equipment supply with limited scope EPC. 
Predictive maintenance, real-time

optimisation of asset availability and

contributing to the successful delivery of 
our lifecycle asset management services.We offer uninterrupted asset support

Our Products and Services
Powering Performance, Delivering 
Advanced Solutions
We deliver integrated wind energy solutions that 
span advanced wind turbine generators, project 
development, EPC, and long-term operations and 
maintenance services. 
Our wind turbines are specifically designed to perform efficiently in the low wind speed conditions prevalent in India, delivering reliable, 
cost-effective and high-performance solutions. Bolstered by consistent product innovation and advanced manufacturing capabilities, 
we supply reliable, efficient and future-ready wind energy solutions.Our integrated service portfolio supports customers across every stage of the wind 
energy project lifecycle, from project planning and development to long-term asset 
management.  By pairing specialised technical skill with flawless execution, we 
deliver end-to-end solutions that elevate project efficiency, operational performance 
and asset reliability. 
We conduct wind and solar resource 
studies, site assessments and technical 
evaluations to identify suitable project 
locations to undertake well-informed 
decision-making for project planning from 
the initial stages of execution.
We uncompromisingly extend our help to 
our customers through technical services, 
operational assistance, performance 
enhancement initiatives and lifecycle 
solutions that improve long-term asset 
reliability and operational efficiency.We facilitate land identification, 
acquisition and statutory approvals 
while preparing project sites to monitor 
timely development and efficient project 
execution.We develop evacuation infrastructure, 
substations and associated site facilities 
to strengthen grid connectivity, improve 
project readiness and support reliable 
power evacuation.
We provide integrated EPC and 
commissioning services, permitting 
seamless execution of wind, hybrid, BESS 
and renewable energy projects through a 
single-point delivery approach.
We deliver long-term asset management 
through remote monitoring, predictive 
maintenance, field service support and 
performance optimisation, accelerating 
augmentation of turbine accessibility 
throughout the asset lifecycle.A proven wind turbine platform 
engineered for reliable performance 
across diverse wind conditions. Built 
on Double Fed Induction Generator 
(DFIG) technology and available in 
multiple hub-height configurations, 
offering dependable energy 
generation, operational reliability and 
simplified maintenance across a wide 
range of project sites.Designed to maximise energy 
generation under low wind speed 
conditions, our 3.3 MW platform 
combines a 145 m rotor diameter 
with an optimised aerodynamic 
design to enhance energy 
yield, operational efficiency and 
project economics. This platform 
supports a substantial share of our 
commercial installations.Representing the next phase of 
our product evolution, the 4.X MW 
platform has been developed to 
address future market requirements 
through higher generation capacity, 
improved energy output and 
enhanced project economics. It 
moreover, strengthens our strategy 
of expanding into higher-capacity 
turbine offerings.Backed by in-house manufacturing capabilities and steady product innovation, we 
remain focused on delivering reliable, efficient and future-ready renewable energy 
solutions that address evolving customer requirements.

Executive Director’s Message
Navigating Change, 
Creating Value
It gives me great pleasure to present INOX 
Wind’s Annual Report for FY2025–26. I 
am happy to inform that over the past few 
years, we have transformed the business 
while building one of the country’s most 
integrated renewable energy groups. The 
progress we have made is the result of 
disciplined execution, the dedication of 
our people and the continued trust of our 
shareholders, customers, lenders and 
business partners. As we build on this 
momentum and deliver on our plans, I am 
confident that the Company is entering 
a new phase of growth with a strong 
foundation already in place.
Why Wind Matters More Than 
Ever
India’s wind power generation sector 
continues to build upon its momentum 
from the previous year. As you are aware, 
FY26 saw the highest ever wind power 
generation capacity addition of 6.05 GW.  
Going forward, we expect to see strong 
annual wind capacity addition of 8-10 
GW over the next few years driven by 
RTC / FDRE / hybrid capacity additions, 
as discoms increasingly want renewable 
power to be a source of firm power.
The ongoing geo-political tensions have 
provided further tailwinds to the entire 
ecosystem of the renewable power sector, 
right from equipment manufacturing to 
renewable power generation capacity. As 
you are aware, there is a strong push from 
the Government to increase domestic 
manufacturing and reduce import 
dependencies.
A Year of Strong Delivery
FY2025-26 was a year of strong financial 
performance, with consolidated revenue 
growing by 23% and EBITDA and Cash 
PAT increasing by more than 25% over the 
previous year. During the year, the merger 
of INOX Wind Energy Limited with INOX 
Wind simplified our corporate structure 
by removing the holding company and 
reducing liabilities by approximately 
H2,050 crore. Together with the successful 
completion of a H1,249 crore rights issue, this resulted in a net cash-positive 
balance sheet. We also continue to have a 
strong credit rating across both short-
term and long-term facilities, reflecting the 
Company’s financial discipline.
Stronger Together 
INOXGFL Group is extremely well placed 
to benefit from and contribute toward 
achieving these goals. We are one of 
the most integrated players in energy 
transition in the country today, given our 
strong presence in the entire value chain, 
right from manufacturing of wind turbines, 
solar cells & modules and transformers, 
EPC including development of evacuation 
infrastructure, RE IPP and renewable 
energy O&M (including through our Group 
Company). We are also further backward 
integrating into power electronics in a big 
way.
INOXGFL renewables adopts ‘ONE 
INTEGRATED’ strategy, where the virtuous 
cycle of inter-play within Group entities 
will aid execution and provide multi-year 
revenue visibility for INOX Wind and its 
subsidiaries. Given Group company INOX 
Clean Energy’s large capacity addition 
plans, with a targeted capacity addition of 
14 GW by FY29, we expect approximately 
one-third of our annual execution targets 
for the next few years to come from INOX 
Clean and the remaining from our other 
marquee customers, including repeat 
and new customers. INOX Wind recently 
signed a multi-year MOU with INOX Clean 
for supply of 1.5 GW wind turbines. Given 
our comfortable order book size of ~4.4 
GW (as on July 2026), we will be selective 
in taking new external orders.
Meanwhile, INOX Green continues to 
expand its O&M portfolio, which has 
grown to over 13 GWp, and remains 
on course to become India’s largest 
renewable O&M company.
Further, we received approval from the 
NCLT for the  demerger of the evacuation 
business from INOX Green into IRSL 
during the year, paving the way for the automatic listing of IRSL on the stock 
exchanges. 
Launch of our 4.X MW wind 
turbines
As we get closer to the launch of our new 
4.X MW turbines, we are pleased to inform 
you that the process is moving forward 
smoothly and we expect to receive all 
approvals and subsequently commercially 
launch the product within this calendar 
year. This would be a milestone in the 
Company’s history and help us penetrate 
deeper into the market as well as lead to 
margin improvement.
Ready for the Next Chapter
As we step into FY2026–27, we believe 
that the inter-play of Group synergies 
would be our next engine of growth. 
All our strategic decisions related to 
backward and forward integration have 
started to yield results.  As India’s energy 
transition gathers pace, we believe INOX 
Wind is well placed to play an even bigger 
role in the years ahead.
I would like to thank our shareholders 
for the trust they continue to place in 
our Group companies and in us. My 
sincere thanks also go to our customers, 
employees and business partners for their 
belief in our vision and for the dedication 
they bring every day. Together, we have 
built a strong foundation, and I look 
forward to what we can achieve in the 
years ahead.
Warm regards,
Devansh Jain

Group CEO’s Message
Charting the 
Way Forward
It is my privilege to present INOX Wind’s 
Annual Report for FY2025–26, a year that 
marked an important chapter for both 
India’s renewable energy sector and our 
Company. India recorded its highest-ever 
annual wind capacity addition of 6.05 
GW, signalling the beginning of a new 
growth cycle driven by supportive policy 
measures and rising demand for firm 
clean energy. Against this encouraging 
backdrop, we delivered a year of strong 
financial performance, strategic progress 
and operational excellence, strengthening 
our position as one of India’s leading 
integrated wind energy solutions 
providers.
Continuing Momentum for Wind 
Energy
India’s wind energy journey has entered 
an exciting new chapter and we see 
immense opportunity ahead. As the 
share of intermittent energy supply in 
the grid has risen to approx. 15% in FY26 
(wind + solar), there is a strong demand 
from discoms for a reliable supply of 
clean energy. Hence, we are seeing 
more RTC / FDRE tenders. Since wind 
forms about 20-30% of these tenders, 
there is strong structural momentum 
for wind power capacity addition in the 
country. Alongside this, the growing 
global emphasis on energy security and 
renewable self-reliance is unlocking fresh 
investment and reinforcing India’s position 
as a leading destination for wind energy 
development.
Delivering Growth with 
Financial Strength
FY2025–26 reflected the strength 
and resilience of our business. While 
geopolitical tensions in West Asia 
temporarily disrupted logistics and 
delayed certain ECS supplies, our 
disciplined execution enabled us to 
deliver another year of strong financial 
performance. 
On a consolidated basis, total income 
increased by 23% year on year to H4,569 crore. EBITDA grew by 25% to H1,232 crore, 
driven by sustained margin expansion 
and the benefits of our backward 
integration strategy. Cash PAT rose by 
28% to H1,032 crore, while PAT stood at 
H449 crore. Equally important, our net 
cash balance sheet gives us the financial 
flexibility to invest with confidence, pursue 
new opportunities and strengthen our 
long-term growth trajectory. 
Building Scale, Strengthening 
Capabilities
Our order book is a strong reflection 
of the trust our customers place in our 
capabilities. With a diversified order book 
of ~4.4 GW (as on July 2026), providing 
execution visibility of more than 24 - 36 
months, we are well positioned for the 
next phase of growth. 
Building capacity has been a strategic 
priority throughout the year. We 
commissioned a new nacelle and hub 
manufacturing facility at Kalyangad, near 
Ahmedabad, significantly strengthening 
our production capabilities. We expect 
to start manufacturing higher capacity 
transformers in this calendar year. We 
have deployed four cranes for in-house 
operations and have placed orders for 
two more cranes. We also have plans 
to enter into high value added power 
electronics products. Collectively, 
these initiatives enhance our cost 
competitiveness, execution capabilities 
and strategic self-reliance.
Powering the Next Generation 
of Wind Energy
Innovation has always been central to our 
growth strategy. Today, we manufacture 
and supply both 2 MW and 3.3 MW 
turbines, with demand increasingly 
shifting towards higher-capacity 
platforms. During the year, we have 
made significant progress in developing 
our 4.X MW turbine. ALMM certification 
is currently under process, and we are 
targeting its commercial launch within 
this calendar year. This next-generation platform will broaden our market 
opportunities while supporting stronger 
profitability.
Poised for the Next
We enter FY2026–27 with confidence, 
backed by a clear strategy and a stronger 
operating platform. Our strong order 
book, the ramp-up of our Kalyangad 
manufacturing facility and the anticipated 
commercial launch of our 4.X MW turbine 
platform provide a strong foundation for 
the year ahead.
We also expect to benefit from the 
growing contribution of our Group 
Company, INOX Clean Energy, whose 
annual capacity addition programme 
is projected to exceed 3 GW, with wind 
projects accounting for 20–30% of the 
portfolio. This creates recurring multi-year 
order visibility from within the Group, 
complementing our growing order 
pipeline.
As we look to the future, our priorities are 
clear. We will strengthen our technology 
leadership, deepen our manufacturing 
capabilities and create sustainable 
value for our shareholders and every 
stakeholder who has placed their trust 
in us. On behalf of the leadership team, 
we thank our shareholders for their 
constant support and extend our sincere 
appreciation to our customers, partners 
and employees, whose dedication and 
belief in our vision continue to drive our 
success. 
Sincerely,
Kailash Lal Tarachandani
Group Chief Executive Officer-

Embodying Excellence,

India’s renewable energy landscape consistently generates favourable 
opportunities for our business, backed by strong demand from discoms, policy-
led capacity expansion, rising demand for reliable clean power and continued 
investments in transmission infrastructure. 
India’s focus on expanding renewable 
energy capacity is anticipated to drive 
long-term demand for wind energy 
solutions. The increasing scale of 
renewable capacity additions generates 
opportunities across our integrated 
business model, spanning wind turbine 
manufacturing, Engineering, Procurement 
and Construction (EPC) execution and 
long-term O&M.Sustained investments in transmission 
infrastructure and power evacuation will 
improve renewable energy integration 
thereby, supporting swifter project 
implementation. Our capabilities in 
renewable infrastructure development, 
substations and EPC execution further 
position us to benefit from this expanding 
ecosystem.Geopolitical developments, including the 
West Asia conflict, continue to reshape 
global energy priorities. While short-term 
volatility in supply chains and commodity 
prices may impact project economics, the 
escalating emphasis on energy security 
is driving key investments in renewable 
energy, domestic manufacturing 
and import substitution, thereby, 
strengthening the long-term outlook for 
enterprises with integrated manufacturing 
and execution capabilities alike.
The increasing share of wind, hybrid 
and Firm and Dispatchable Renewable

turnkey execution capabilities and 
foraying into hybrid project opportunities 
through our Group ecosystem. With our integrated manufacturing, project execution and lifecycle service capabilities, we remain well positioned to capitalise on these 
long-term industry trends that enhances our long-term growth.

modules, alongside end-to-end EPC and O&M solutions.

approach to weaving sustainability into 
governance systems, business strategy, 
and daily operations. It reflects our

and governance (ESG) responsibilities,

Our operations Four distinctive business models
IWL forms an integral part of the 
INOXGFL Group — one of India’s 
foremost business conglomerates, 
with a market capitalization of US$ 16 
billion. Backed by a legacy spanning 
over a century, the Group operates 
across diversified business segments, 
including Refrigerants, Fluoropolymers, 
Speciality Chemicals, and Wind Energy 
& Renewables.Inox Wind Limited (IWL) is India’s leading wind energy solutions provider, playing a 
pivotal role in advancing the country’s renewable energy landscape.
At its core, IWL is a fully integrated player 
in the wind energy sector, operating five 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities 
strategically located across Gujarat,  
Madhya Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh, 
with a combined manufacturing capacity 
of 2.5 GW. The company manufactures 
key components of Wind Turbine 
Generators (WTGs) in-house, enabling 
superior quality control, technological 
GRI 2. D. 2.1: - Organisational detailsadvancement, reliability, and cost 
competitiveness. Purpose-built for low 
wind-speed sites across India, Inox Wind’s  
WTGs reflect the company’s ongoing 
commitment to delivering sustainable and 
efficient energy solutions.
Inox Wind Limited offers comprehensive turnkey solutions for 
renewable power projects, providing end-to-end services across 
the entire project lifecycle—from project conceptualization and 
development to commissioning and long-term operation and 
maintenance. Leveraging its integrated business model, the Company 
delivers a wide range of services, including resource assessment, 
energy yield analysis, land acquisition, site infrastructure development, 
power evacuation, statutory approvals and clearances, as well as the 
supply, installation, and commissioning of Wind Turbine Generators 
(WTGs) and solar modules.
By offering an integrated suite of solutions under a single platform, the 
Company ensures seamless project execution, enhanced operational 
efficiency, optimized costs, and timely project delivery. This approach 
enables customers to benefit from a streamlined implementation 
process while maximizing the long-term performance and reliability of 
their renewable energy assetsTurnkey Solutions
In addition to the supply of Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs), Inox Wind 
Limited offers flexible and customizable service solutions, enabling 
customers to select specific services or an integrated package 
based on their project requirements. This customer-centric approach 
enhances project efficiency, optimizes resource utilization, and ensures 
the effective delivery of solutions tailored to the unique requirements of 
each wind power project. Equipment Supply SolutionsLimited Scope Solutions
Under this business model, Inox Wind Limited (IWL) supplies Wind 
Turbine Generators (WTGs) and other associated equipment to 
customers, while the remaining project development activities—including 
wind resource assessment, energy yield analysis, land acquisition, site 
infrastructure development, power evacuation, and statutory approvals—
are undertaken by the customers or their designated agencies. Based 
on project-specific requirements, customers may also engage IWL to 
provide selected services from its portfolio.
Where requested, IWL additionally undertakes the erection, foundation 
casting, testing, and commissioning of wind farms, offering customers 
the flexibility to avail standalone services or an integrated execution 
package tailored to their project needs through its subsidiary, Inox 
Renewable Solutions Limited.Equipment Supply Solutions
Inox Wind Limited’s subsidiary, Inox Green Energy Services Limited 
provides comprehensive Operation & Maintenance (O&M) services 
for wind energy assets and the associated Balance of Plant (BoP), 
ensuring reliable operations and sustained asset performance 
throughout the project lifecycle. With an O&M portfolio of ~ 13.3 GWp 
(including investments made, one of which is under consolidation) , the 
Company leverages its experienced field teams, advanced monitoring 
systems, and established maintenance practices to optimize turbine 
availability and operational efficiency.
The O&M services include 24×7 remote monitoring, predictive and 
preventive maintenance, condition monitoring, scheduled inspections, 
breakdown maintenance, spare parts management, and timely 
corrective interventions. By adopting a proactive maintenance 
approach, Inox Wind Limited enhances asset reliability, maximizes 
energy generation, extends equipment life, and delivers long-term 
value to its customers.O&M Services

Governance

Our Leadership Structure
At Inox Wind Limited, strong corporate 
governance forms the foundation 
of sustainable value creation and 
responsible business conduct. The 
Company is committed to maintaining the 
highest standards of governance through 
ethical business practices, transparency, 
accountability, and compliance with 
applicable laws and regulations. As a 
part of the Inox GFL Group, the Company 
upholds the Group's core values and 
governance philosophy, fostering a 
culture of integrity, responsible decision-
making, and long-term stakeholder value.
The Board of Directors provides strategic 
direction and exercises effective oversight 
over the Company's affairs. Comprising 
members with diverse professional 
expertise and industry experience, the 
Board brings a balanced perspective to 
governance, risk management, business 
strategy, and long-term growth. Through 
its collective experience and independent 
judgment, the Board ensures that the 
Company's operations are aligned with its 
strategic objectives while safeguarding 
the interests of all stakeholders.
As on March 31, 2026, the Board 
comprised six Directors, including two Executive Directors, one Non-Executive 
Non-Independent Director, and three Non-
Executive Independent Directors, including 
one Woman Independent Director. The 
composition of the Board reflects the 
Company's commitment to maintaining an 
appropriate balance between executive 
and independent oversight, thereby 
strengthening transparency, accountability, 
and effective governance.
The Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee (NRC) oversees the 
appointment of Directors and senior 
leadership through a structured and 
transparent selection process. While 
evaluating potential candidates, the 
Committee considers a broad range 
of attributes, including professional 
competence, industry knowledge, 
leadership capabilities, integrity, diversity 
of skills and experience, independence, 
and alignment with the Company's 
strategic priorities and values. This 
approach enables the Company to 
maintain a diverse, competent, and 
future-ready Board capable of addressing 
evolving business opportunities and risks.
The Board is supported by its various 
Committees, which facilitate focused 
oversight of key areas including audit and financial reporting, risk management, 
nomination and remuneration, 
stakeholder relationship management, 
and corporate social responsibility. These 
Committees operate under clearly defined 
terms of reference and report regularly 
to the Board, thereby enhancing the 
overall effectiveness of the Company’s 
governance framework.
The Company’s governance structure 
is further strengthened by its Key 
Managerial Personnel (KMP), comprising 
the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief 
Financial Officer (CFO), and Company 
Secretary (CS). Together, they are 
responsible for driving operational 
excellence, ensuring financial discipline, 
maintaining regulatory compliance, 
implementing strategic initiatives, and 
supporting the Board in achieving the 
Company’s long-term objectives.
Through a robust governance framework, 
effective leadership, and a culture of 
ethics and accountability, Inox Wind 
Limited remains committed to creating 
sustainable value for its stakeholders 
while ensuring resilience, responsible 
growth, and long-term business success.

Supply Chain & 
Procurement RisksRisks relating to the availability, quality, pricing, and timely procurement of critical raw 
materials and components, as well as supplier performance and geopolitical disruptions.
Project Execution RisksRisks associated with delays in land acquisition, statutory approvals, grid connectivity, 
logistics, construction, commissioning, and customer acceptance of projects.
Operational & Asset 
Performance RisksRisks related to turbine reliability, equipment failure, asset availability, maintenance

Technology & Product 
Innovation RisksRisks arising from rapid technological advancements, product obsolescence, evolving

Quality & Product Liability 
RisksRisks related to product quality, manufacturing defects, warranty obligations, certification 
requirements, and customer claims.
Business Continuity RisksRisks arising from natural disasters, pandemics, industrial accidents, utility disruptions, 
geopolitical events, or other unforeseen incidents affecting operations.
Environmental, Health & 
Safety (EHS) RisksRisks relating to environmental compliance, occupational health and safety, hazardous 
materials management, and workplace incidents across manufacturing sites and project 
locations.
Human Capital RisksRisks associated with talent acquisition, retention, succession planning, employee capability 
development, workforce productivity, and employee engagement.
Information Security & 
Cybersecurity RisksRisks arising from cyber threats, data privacy breaches, ransomware attacks, operational

"Transparency in Compensation: Annual Pay Ratio Disclosure"
Inox Wind Limited believes that transparent and responsible remuneration practices are fundamental to good corporate governance 
and sustainable business performance. The Annual Compensation Ratio, which compares the annual remuneration of the highest-
paid individual with the median remuneration of all employees, provides stakeholders with insight into the Company's compensation 
structure and pay equity.
Disclosure of this metric reflects the Company's commitment to transparency, fairness, and accountability in its remuneration 
practices. It also enables stakeholders to better understand the distribution of compensation across the organization while supporting 
alignment with applicable ESG reporting frameworks and promoting responsible and equitable reward practices.

Fair Wages and Responsible Compensation
At Inox Wind Limited, we believe that

social equity, and sustainable business

permanent workers received wages 
above the applicable statutory minimum 
wages prescribed under the relevant

of recognising employee contributions through competitive compensation 
while supporting financial security and 
improved quality of life.
For other than permanent employees 
and workers, remuneration is 
administered in accordance with 
applicable minimum wage notifications 
through authorised contractors. 
The Company monitors contractor 
compliance with statutory wage 
obligations and expects all contracting 
partners to adhere to applicable labour 
laws, fair employment practices, and 
employee welfare requirements.
While compliance with statutory minimum 
wages forms the foundation of our 
compensation framework, we recognise that sustainable livelihoods extend 
beyond legal compliance. Accordingly, 
we continue to periodically review our 
compensation philosophy in line with 
evolving market conditions, business 
requirements, employee expectations, 
and emerging ESG practices. As part of 
our long-term sustainability journey, we 
remain committed to strengthening our 
remuneration practices and evaluating 
opportunities to progressively align with 
broader living wage principles wherever 
feasible.
These initiatives reflect our commitment 
to promoting decent work, supporting 
employee well-being, and creating long-
term social value for our workforce and 
the communities in which we operate.

Management

Management Discussion and Analysis
Economic Overview
Global Economy1
The global economy in CY 2025 operated within a complex 
macroeconomic environment characterised by geopolitical 
tensions, shifting trade dynamics and structural supply chain 
realignments. Throughout the year, manufacturing and logistics 
sectors proactively adapted to evolving trade dynamics and 
tariff recalibrations, encouraging healthy diversification of 
sourcing and a renewed emphasis on regional self-reliance. This 
evolution proved particularly beneficial for regions with localised 
manufacturing footprints, facilitating efficient trade routes and 
mitigating external volatility, ensuring essential goods and energy 
components continued to flow uninterrupted. Despite these 
headwinds, the global output expanded by 3.5%, supported by 
policy interventions and sustained momentum in technology-
related investment. However, growth in advanced economies 
moderated to 1.9% in CY 2025, whereas emerging market and 
developing economies achieved higher growth at 4.5%, supported 
by technology-enabled trade flows across Asia.
Outlook
Global growth is projected to moderate to 3.0% in CY 2026, 
before a modest recovery to 3.4% in CY 2027, weighed down by 
geopolitical disruptions, elevated commodity prices and persistent structural constraints. Global headline inflation is projected at 4.4% 
in CY 2026, driven by rising energy and food prices. While active 
hostilities in the Middle East have eased, the region continues 
to present geopolitical risks to the global outlook, with potential 
implications for commodity markets, inflation expectations and 
financial stability. Although immediate concerns over disruptions 
to major energy infrastructure and critical trade routes, including 
the Strait of Hormuz, have moderated, any renewed escalation 
could materially affect global hydrocarbon supply and intensify 
energy market pressures. Growth prospects remain uneven, 
leaving emerging and developing economies that are net 
commodity importers particularly vulnerable to inflationary 
pressures, currency volatility and external shocks.
Emerging markets are expected to remain the primary 
contributors to global economic growth, driven by strong domestic 
consumption and expansion in the services sector. Meanwhile, 
advanced economies are likely to witness a gradual recovery, 
supported by disciplined monetary policies and improving 
investment conditions for capital-intensive industries. The global 
focus on energy security and sustainable infrastructure remains a 
primary driver of long-term growth. Technological innovation and 
operational excellence, on the other hand, contribute to a stable 
and prosperous economic future.

Indian Economy
India sustained its position among the world's fastest-growing 
major economies during FY 2025-26, with real GDP growth at 7.7%, driven primarily by resilient domestic demand. Private consumption and capital formation remained the twin engines of this expansion, while the services sector continued to be the largest contributor on the supply side. Manufacturing activity gained further momentum; in contrast, agriculture provided stability despite persistent structural constraints. Consumer price inflation moderated to 3.4%, allowing the Reserve Bank of India to reduce the policy repo rate by a cumulative 100 basis points. 
On the fiscal side, the Union Budget 2025-26 introduced direct tax 
relief for the middle-income segment, aimed at lifting disposable incomes and encouraging discretionary spending. Rationalisation of the GST framework lent further support to MSMEs and the informal sector. The Government sustained its emphasis on infrastructure-led development, allocating capital expenditure of ₹11.21 lakh crore in the Union Budget 2025-26, while advancing its clean energy priorities. India also made significant progress in renewable energy deployment, reinforcing the credibility of its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) commitments. Continued expansion of solar and wind capacity, supported by enabling policy measures and increased investment in clean energy infrastructure, has strengthened the country's transition towards a low-carbon economy.
India's renewable energy push received a significant boost 
through the Domestic Content Requirements (DCR) policy and the shift toward Hybrid and Round-the-Clock (RTC) tenders. These measures are aimed at strengthening grid reliability and domestic manufacturing. By March 2026, total installed renewable capacity reached 274.68 GW, with solar crossing 150 GW. On the international commitments front, India reportedly fulfilled its Paris Agreement target of 50% non-fossil fuel capacity five years ahead of its 2030 deadline.

monetary policy stance and repo rate held at 5.25% whereas CPI inflation is projected at 5.1% for FY27.

Industry Overview
Global Energy Sector5
In 2025, global renewable power capacity reached 5,149 GW, 
following the addition of 692 GW during the year. This marked 
a 15.5% increase and the fastest annual growth on record. The 
sector is undergoing structural change, underpinned by declining 
levelized costs of energy and policy frameworks promoting net 
zero emissions, driving investments in wind, solar PV, wind and 
battery storage. A key trend is the digitalisation of energy assets, 
enabling virtual power plants and improved grid management, 
while challenges such as integrating intermittent sources and 
supply chain risks for critical minerals like polysilicon remain.6Low-
emissions technologies, comprising solar, wind, nuclear and 
hydropower, collectively accounted for nearly 60% of global 
energy demand growth. In a historic milestone, solar PV emerged 
as the single largest contributor to global energy supply growth, 
accounting for over 25% of the increase. 
The wind energy sector recorded a milestone year with 165 GW 
of new capacity additions globally, representing a 40% increase. 
Growth was primarily driven by onshore demand in China, the 
USA and India, highlighting the sector’s ability to scale rapidly 
while delivering cost-competitive and resilient energy solutions. 
Supported by continued expansion across Asia, wind power is 
increasingly competitive with conventional energy sources such 
as coal and nuclear, reinforcing its role in accelerating the energy 
transition. Moreover, annual wind installations are projected to 
reach a record 178 GW in 2026. Supported by existing policy 
frameworks and the global response to the Middle East crisis, 
cumulative new wind capacity additions are expected to total 969 
GW during 2026–2030, averaging approximately 194 GW annually, 
maintaining a robust CAGR of 5.2% over the 2026–2030 period.7Outlook
Looking ahead, renewable energy capacity is expected to sustain 
robust growth through 2030, with the combined share of solar 
PV and wind projected to increase from 17% of global generation 
in 2025 to 27% by 2030. Beyond capacity expansion, the industry 
focus is increasingly shifting toward the structural modernisation 
of power systems to accommodate higher shares of variable 
energy. This transition is being supported by the rapid scale-up 
of battery storage solutions and the expansion of smart grid 
infrastructure to ensure long-term reliability and grid stability. As 
renewable technologies continue to mature, they are expected to 
play a pivotal role in advancing global industrial electrification and 
strengthening energy security.8

Global wind energy sector9
The global wind energy sector delivered a record-breaking 
performance in CY 2025, with 165 GW of new capacity installed 
worldwide, representing a 40% year-on-year increase. This took 
cumulative global wind capacity to 1,299 GW. The Asia-Pacific 
region remained the primary growth driver, accounting for 80% of 
new installations. Growth was led by China, which recorded close 
to 120 GW of new capacity additions, while India added 6.34 GW 
of new onshore wind capacity, reflecting an 85% increase year-
on-year increase. Europe also crossed the significant milestone 
of 300 GW in cumulative installed wind capacity, adding 19.1 GW 
during the year. Meanwhile, Africa and the Middle East recorded 
a 32% increase in new capacity additions, reflecting growing 
adoption across emerging markets.
Outlook
According to GWEC Market Intelligence, global wind installations 
are projected to reach 178 GW by the end of 2026 and average 
approximately 194 GW annually through 2030, resulting in nearly 
969 GW of cumulative additions during the period. This growth 
outlook is supported by China’s 15th Five-Year Plan, which targets 
annual installations of at least 120 GW. In addition, global offshore

India’s Renewable Energy
India’s renewable energy sector maintained strong momentum 
during FY 2025-26, recording the highest-ever annual addition 
of non-fossil fuel capacity at 55.29 GW. Total renewable energy 
installed capacity increased to 274.68 GW as of March 31, 2026, 
while total non-fossil fuel capacity reached 283.46 GW11. Solar 
energy remained the primary growth driver during the year. 
Record solar capacity additions of 44.61 GW increased cumulative 
installed solar capacity to 150.26 GW. Wind energy also recorded 
its highest-ever annual addition of 6.05 GW, taking cumulative 
installed wind capacity to 56.09 GW.
Sector growth continued to be supported by favourable policy 
measures, including the reduction in GST on renewable energy 
equipment from 12% to 5%, expansion of domestic manufacturing 
under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) and 
continued transmission support measures. During FY 2025–26, 
India also achieved the milestone of deriving 50% of its cumulative 
installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources, five 
years ahead of its Paris Agreement target. The country now ranks 
third globally in renewable energy installed capacity.Outlook
India’s renewable energy sector is expected to sustain strong long-
term growth momentum, supported by the Government’s target 
of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed capacity 
by 2030. Policy focus continues to remain on strengthening 
transmission infrastructure, expanding domestic manufacturing 
capabilities and accelerating deployment of hybrid and round-
the-clock (RTC) renewable energy projects.
In parallel, initiatives such as Green Energy Open Access, 
expansion of renewable energy corridors and continued support 
for domestic battery manufacturing are expected to improve 
grid integration and enhance renewable energy adoption across 
utility-scale and commercial & industrial segments. The National 
Green Hydrogen Mission is also expected to support incremental 
renewable capacity addition over the medium term.

Source: MNRE / PIB Release ID 2250039.India’s Wind Energy Sector16
India’s wind energy sector remains one of the largest globally, 
ranking fourth in installed capacity. During FY 2025-26, the 
country recorded its highest-ever annual wind capacity addition 
of approximately 6 GW, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth. 
Cumulative installed wind capacity surpassed 56 GW, reinforcing 
India’s position as a key global wind energy market. Capacity 
additions continue to be concentrated across leading states 
such as Gujarat, Karnataka and Maharashtra. Sector growth was 
further supported by an expanding pipeline of wind-solar hybrid 
projects and the implementation of Green Energy Open Access 
regulations. Policy support remained favourable during the year, 
including concessional customs duties on key components 
and the waiver of Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) 
charges until June 2028. The sector also benefits from a well-
established domestic manufacturing ecosystem, with an annual 
manufacturing capacity of approximately 24 GW and high levels of 
indigenisation. However, structural challenges persist, particularly 
in relation to grid connectivity, transmission infrastructure, RoW 
issues and land acquisition. These areas continue to be critical, 
requiring sustained policy and infrastructure support.
Outlook
India’s wind sector is expected to witness sustained long-term 
growth, supported by favourable policy measures and continued 
technological advancements. The Government has set ambitious 
targets, including 100 GW of installed wind capacity by 2030, 
aligned with the broader objective of reaching 500 GW of non-
fossil fuel energy capacity. The increasing adoption of hybrid and 
round-the-clock (RTC) renewable energy solutions is expected to 
improve grid stability and optimise resource utilisation, alongside 
driving demand for wind energy. In addition, India’s significant 
wind potential at higher hub heights provides a strong foundation 
for long-term capacity expansion.
Government Initiatives to Support India’s Clean Energy 
Transition
The Union Budget for FY 2026–27 allocated approximately 
₹32,915 crore to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy 
(MNRE), reflecting continued policy emphasis on accelerating 
India’s clean energy transition. Further, the Government has 
approved an additional Rs. 30,000 crores investment in the 
National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) in June 
2026. The increased allocation underscores the Government’s 
sustained commitment toward renewable energy deployment. 
The Government continues to target 100 GW of installed wind 
capacity by 2030 as part of its broader objective of achieving 
500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based energy capacity. These targets 
remain central to India’s long-term decarbonisation and energy 
security strategy.
Policy support for renewable energy evacuation also remains 
strong. Waivers on Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) charges 
continue to support project viability, particularly for wind and 
hybrid energy projects. In parallel, regulatory mechanisms, such 
as Renewable Consumption Obligations, are being implemented 
to ensure sustained demand for renewable power across states.

Company Overview
Inox Wind Limited (IWL) operates as one of India’s leading fully 
integrated wind energy solution providers. As a key entity of the 
INOXGFL Group, the Company deliveres end-to-end solutions 
spanning project development, manufacturing, execution and 
long-term operations and maintenance (O&M).  The Company 
possesses over 17 years of operational experience and has a 
manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GW across five specialised facilities. 
It manufactures 2 MW and 3 MW Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) 
and has a license for 4 MW platform, with a 4.45 MW commercial 
launch in FY27. It benefits from a strong promoter backing and 
has a robust and diversified order book of approximately 4.4 
GW as on July 2026. Its subsidiary, Inox Green Energy Services 
Limited (IGESL), is a leading renewable energy O&M service 
provider, managing a portfolio of ~13.3 GWp as on June’26 
across wind and solar assets. Another subsidiary, Inox Renewable 
Solutions Limited (IRSL), provides turnkey as well as limited scope EPC services, including resource assessment, site acquisition, 
infrastructure development, crane services and transformer 
manufacturing, with plans to enter manufacturing of power 
electronics such as inverters. The Company also collaborates 
with Group entity Inox Clean Energy to offer integrated hybrid, 
BESS and solar power solutions. Manufacturing operations for 
nacelles and hubs are carried out at Una (HP), Bhuj (Gujarat), and 
the newly commissioned Bavla facility (near Ahmedabad). Blades 
and tubular towers are manufactured at plants located at Rohika 
(Gujarat) and Barwani (MP). These facilities enable in-house 
production of all critical turbine components specifically designed 
for India’s low wind speed regimes. The Company achieved a 
major corporate milestone with the merger of Inox Wind Energy 
Limited into IWL, which eliminated the holding company structure 
and reduced liabilities by approximately ₹2,050 crores. Supported 
by a successful ₹1,249 crore rights issue, the transition enabled 
the Company to achieve a net-cash-positive balance sheet.

Key Differentiating Factors
One of the Most Integrated Renewable Energy Players in India  
Inox Wind Limited operates as a fully integrated, end-to-end 
renewable energy solutions provider for the entire value chain. 
Its capabilities cover project site identification, acquisition, 
resource assessment, manufacturing, EPC execution and long-
term O&M services. By managing the complete project lifecycle, 
the Company ensures seamless plug-and-play execution for 
customers. This integrated approach reduces execution risks and 
provides a competitive advantage over OEMs focused solely on 
equipment supply.
Net-Cash-Positive Capital Structure
The Company continues to remain net cash positive as on Mar’26 
with a strong balance sheet and enjoys an extremely healthy 
credit rating of AA- (long term). Short term credit rating of A1+ 
(highest short term rating). The strong financial position enables 
the Company to scale up operations in line with the massive 
market opportunity.
Technological Advancement and 4X MW Platform Readiness
The Company continues to strengthen its technology roadmap 
through long-term technology-sharing agreements with global 
partners such as AMSC, W2E, etc. While the 3 MW WTG platform 
is the primary product offering at present, the Company has 
secured licenses and is progressing well toward commercial 
launch of the 4.45 MW platform in CY2026. These turbines are 
specifically engineered to optimise energy yield in India’s low wind 
speed conditions. The introduction of higher-capacity turbines is 
expected to significantly improve the Levelized Cost of Energy 
(LCOE) for project developers.
Scaled Manufacturing Presence with Geographic 
Diversification
The Company has a manufacturing footprint of 2.5 GW of annual 
capacity across strategically located facilities. During the year, 
the newly commissioned Bavla nacelle and hub facility near 
Ahmedabad became fully operational, complementing existing 
manufacturing units in Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat. The 
Company has also undertaken upgrade of blade molds in the 
Madhya Pradesh plant during the year. We are also working on 
the development of a new blade and tower manufacturing facility 
in South India to reduce logistical costs for regional projects. This 
multi-location strategy ensures de-risking, high supply chain 
resilience and compliance with domestic sourcing mandates.
High-Margin Asset-Light Annuity Business from O&M 
Subsidiary
Through its listed subsidiary, Inox Green Energy Services Limited 
(IGESL), the Company has established a very large and diversified 
O&M portfolio. The portfolio of approximately 13+ GWp following 
strategic investments and acquisitions of multi-brand renewable 
energy assets is amongst the largest in the country. Further, IGESL 
is the only listed pure-play renewable O&M player in India. 
Long-term service contracts, ranging from 5 to 20 years, generate 
stable and high-margin annuity cash flows while maintaining 
machine availability levels exceeding 95%. The transition toward a pure-play O&M model also strengthens the Group’s return on 
equity (ROE) and overall capital efficiency. 
Its focus on strong technological capabilities with 24x7 
centralized digital monitoring of assets, focus on preventive 
rather than reactive maintenance and operational optimisation 
has supported high fleet availability. Value-added services, which 
includes refurbishment, booster sales, carbon credit trading, 
amongst other offerings, is another high growth vertical.
Expansion into solar and hybrid asset management further 
strengthens its long-term growth prospects. Strong relationships 
with independent power producers (IPPs), PSUs and commercial 
& industrial clients continue to drive repeat business. The 
O&M segment remains a key pillar of financial stability and 
margin improvement.
End-to-end development and EPC capability through 
subsidiary Inox Renewable Solutions Limited
The Company undertook a strategic restructuring through 
demerging the substation business from Inox Green Energy 
Services Limited (IGESL) into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited 
(IRSL). This scheme of demerger has been approved by the 
Hon’ble NCLT Ahmedabad. IRSL will be automatically listed on 
the stock exchanges post receipt of all approvals. This move 
transformed the O&M business into an asset-light entity while 
consolidating infrastructure services under IRSL. Further, the 
Company is successfully backward integrating. It has started 
manufacturing transformers of upto 3.5 MV A at its factory in 
Jaipur, Rajasthan, with plans to manufacture higher capacity 
transformers in future. The Company now owns and operates 
4 cranes, with plans to deploy more over the next two years. 
Further, the Company is planning to enter into manufacturing 
of high value-added power electronics such as inverters. Such 
backward integration initiatives help the company in faster 
execution, substantial cost savings, improve margins and reduce 
dependence on external vendors. In line with the evolution of the 
renewable energy market in India, IRSL has expanded its service 
offerings beyond plain vanilla wind projects to more complex 
hybrid projects, including Round-the-Clock (RTC) and Firm and 
Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) projects, including solar 
and battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Captive Order Visibility via Group IPP Company (Inox Clean 
Energy)
The Company benefits from a stable demand pipeline through 
its group entity, Inox Clean Energy. This IPP platform has large 
capacity addition plans, with a targeted capacity of 14 GW by 
FY29. It plans to add 3 GW+ capacity annually over the next few 
years. Out of this, about 20-30% is expected to be wind. This is 
expected to provide a virtuous cycle of continuous order inflow to 
the entire value chain of Inox Wind, IRSL and Inox Green over the 
next few years, in addition to order flows in the regular course of 
business. InoxGFL Group’s renewable business is on the cusp of 
multi-year multi-fold growth, with the benefits of Group synergies 
and businesses that help secure large growth and insulate 
from market cycles.
Compliance with ALMM and Domestic Content Requirements

positioning across central and state-level PSU tenders.
Diversified Blue-Chip Customer Base and Robust Order Book
The Company maintains a healthy and diversified order book of 
approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, providing revenue visibility 
for more than two years.* The order pipeline includes projects 
from reputed counterparties, reflecting continued confidence in 
execution capabilities. The customer mix includes major public 
sector undertakings (PSUs) such as NTPC, NLC, GAIL and SJVN, 
along with leading IPP players such as CESC, Gentari, Hero Future 
Energies and Aditya Birla Group. Repeat orders from existing

quality. Geographic diversification across high wind-potential 
states further strengthens the Company’s market presence. The 
Company’s growing participation in hybrid and complex projects 
enhances its relevance in the evolving energy landscape. This 
broad-based presence supports sustainable revenue growth. 
As the Company grows, it is doing a strategic pivot towards

The Company has also seen continued participation from

Operational Efficiency and Technology Focus

focus on digital tools, remote monitoring and data analytics has 
improved asset performance. Operational improvements also 
contributed to stronger cost management and margin stability.

Risk Management and Mitigation Framework
Risk Category Definition and Impact Mitigation Strategy
DFinancial RiskPotential volatility in earnings and 
liquidity arising from fluctuations in 
interest rates, credit availability and 
working capital cycles.The Company eliminated interest-bearing debt and promoter 
preference shares (NCRPS/NCPRPS) through a ₹1,249 crore 
rights issue and the IWEL merger. Achieving a net-cash-
positive position significantly reduced finance costs and 
strengthened the balance sheet against interest rate volatility.
Operational and 
Execution RiskDelays in project commissioning due 
to site readiness issues, logistical 
bottlenecks or infrastructure 
constraints are impacting revenue 
recognition timelines.IWL deployed an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes and 
established a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility to 
ensure end-to-end control. The demerger of the substation 
business into a specialised EPC entity, Inox Renewable 
Solutions Limited (IRSL), enabled focused infrastructure 
development and improved project execution efficiency.
Regulatory and 
Policy RiskChanges in government regulations, 
including ALMM (Wind) mandates 
or revisions in GST rates, may affect 
sector competitiveness and project 
economics.The Company maintained 75-80% domestic sourcing of 
critical components, ensuring early compliance with ALMM 
(Wind) requirements. Proactive localisation of the 3 MW and 
upcoming 4X MW platforms reduced import-related risks 
while enabling the Company to benefit from the reduced 5% 
GST rate applicable to wind energy components.
Technology RiskRisk of product obsolescence or failure 
to meet the evolving energy yield 
requirements of project developers in 
low-wind regimes.The Company secured long-term technology licensing 
agreement with global leaders such as W2E for the 4X MW 
platform. Continued investment in R&D and the planned 
CY2026 commercial launch of the 4.45 MW (4X) platform 
ensure the Company remains at the forefront of LCOE 
optimisation.
Internal Control Systems and Their Adequacy
The Company has established and continues to strengthen a 
comprehensive internal control framework designed to ensure 
the orderly and efficient conduct of its business operations. These 
controls support compliance with applicable laws and regulations, 
safeguard assets, and promote optimal utilisation of resources. 
An independent internal audit function is in place, carried out 
by qualified external Chartered Accountants, to evaluate the 
effectiveness of internal controls, risk management practices and 
governance processes. The internal audit plan is risk-based and is 
reviewed periodically to address evolving business requirements. 
The Audit Committee of the Board provides oversight of the 
internal audit function and regularly reviews audit observations, 
management responses and the status of implementation of 
recommendations. Corrective actions are tracked to closure 
to ensure continuous improvement in control processes. The 
Company also maintains robust financial and management 
reporting systems, which are subject to periodic review and 
enhancement to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of 
information used for decision-making.Disclaimer

skills, experience, expertise, contribution during her tenure 
and continued fulfilment of the criteria of independence,

The Board of Directors, based on the performance evaluation 
of Ms. Madhurima Sayan Das and the recommendation 
of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, is of the 
view that, considering her extensive experience, expertise, 
valuable contribution to the deliberations of the Board and her 
commitment and participation in the affairs of the Company, her 
continued association would be beneficial to the Company and 
its stakeholders.

appointment of Ms. Madhurima Sayan Das as an Independent 
Director of the Company, not liable to retire by rotation, for a second 
term of 1 (one) year commencing from 5th September, 2026.
Section 149(10) of the Act provides that an Independent Director 
shall hold office for a term of upto 5 (five) consecutive years on the 
Board of a company and shall be eligible for re-appointment for a 
second term on passing of a Special Resolution by the Members 
and disclosure of such re-appointment in the Board’s Report.
The Company has received a declaration from Ms. Madhurima 
Sayan Das confirming that she meets the criteria of independence 
prescribed under Section 149(6) of the Act and the Listing 
Regulations. The Company has also received confirmation that 
she is not debarred from holding the office of Director by virtue 
of any order of the Securities and Exchange Board of India or 
any other authority. In the opinion of the Board, she fulfils the 
conditions specified under the Act and the Listing Regulations for 
re-appointment as an Independent Director and is independent of 
the management of the Company.

Item No. 4
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 180(1)(c) of the Companies 
Act, 2013 (“the Act”), the Board of Directors of a company can 
exercise the power to borrow money, where the money to be 
borrowed, together with the money already borrowed by the 
company, will exceed the aggregate of its paid-up share capital, 
free reserves and securities premium, apart from temporary 
loans obtained from the company’s bankers in the ordinary 
course of business, only with the approval of the Members by way 
of a Special Resolution.
The Members of the Company, at the Extra-ordinary General 
Meeting held on 23rd February, 2015, had approved the borrowing 
powers of the Board of Directors upto an aggregate amount of 
H 5,000 Crore. The Company currently has a working capital 
consortium arrangement of H 4,000 Crore, of which approximately 
80% is utilised, along with certain other credit facilities from its 
existing lenders.
Considering the Company's projected business growth, increasing 
working capital requirements, capital expenditure and expansion 
plans, the Company's funding requirements are expected to 
increase significantly in the coming years. The Company may 
also require additional financial flexibility for refinancing existing 
borrowings and meeting other business and corporate funding 
requirements from time to time.
In view of the existing level of sanctioned and utilised credit 
facilities and the anticipated increase in funding requirements, 
the available headroom under the current borrowing limit of  
H 5,000 Crore may not be sufficient to support the Company's 
future business requirements and growth plans. Accordingly, it is 
proposed to increase the borrowing limit of the Company from 
H 5,000 Crore to H 8,000 Crore to provide adequate flexibility 
for raising funds, as and when required, from banks, financial 
institutions and other permissible sources.
The borrowings raised by the Company may, in the ordinary 
course of business, be secured by way of mortgage, charge, 
hypothecation, pledge, lien or other security over the movable 
and/or immovable properties and assets of the Company, in such 
form, manner and ranking as may be determined by the Board 
from time to time in consultation with the lenders.
The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on 7th August, 2026, 
approved the aforesaid proposal.

Item No. 7
Inox Wind Limited ("IWL" or the "Company") is one of India's 
leading integrated wind energy solutions providers engaged 
in the manufacture and supply of wind turbine generators 
("WTGs") and ancillary and incidental equipment. The Company, 
through its subsidiaries is engaged in erection, procurement and 
commissioning (EPC) of WTGs (through Inox Renewable Solutions 
Limited) and the operations and maintenance (O&M) services 
of wind and solar farms (through Inox Green Energy Services 
Limited), enabling it to offer integrated solutions across the 
renewable energy value chain.
The Company forms part of the INOXGFL Group's integrated 
renewable energy platform, under which various Group entities 
are engaged in complementary businesses across the renewable 
energy value chain, including manufacture and supply of 
wind turbine generators and related equipment, engineering, 
procurement and construction services, renewable energy 
project development, operations and maintenance of WTGs and 
solar farms and other allied activities.
Given the integrated nature of the Group's renewable energy 
business, the Company and, wherever applicable, its subsidiaries, 
regularly undertake transactions with various Group entities 
to meet customer requirements, facilitate integrated business 
arrangements, support project execution and operational 
requirements, optimise working capital, treasury and funding 
arrangements and efficiently conduct their business operations. 
These transactions include, inter alia, purchase and sale of goods 
and services, operational and project support arrangements, 
financial accommodations and other commercial arrangements 
required for the efficient conduct of business. In addition, the 
Company may, from time to time, avail financial assistance, from 
its Group entity, Inox Clean Energy Limited and Promoter Director, 
Shri Devansh Jain to meet its fund requirements, if need arises.

The proposed related party transactions arise from the Company's 
business and operational requirements, including integrated 
business arrangements with Group entities and, in the case of 
financial arrangements with the Promoter Director, the Company's 
funding and treasury requirements. The proposed transactions 
are intended to facilitate the efficient conduct and growth of the 
Company's business and provide the Company with appropriate 
operational and financial flexibility. These transactions, inter alia, 
provide the following benefits:
	 Operational efficiency through integration of services, 
procurement and execution across Group entities;
	 Cost optimisation driven by economies of scale, shared 
infrastructure and procurement advantages;
	 Access to technical expertise, execution capabilities and 
specialised resources available within the Group;
	 Enables the Company to deliver integrated turnkey 
renewable energy solutions to customers by leveraging 
synergies, scale and competencies across Group entities:
	 Strategic alignment with the Company's long-term growth 
plans and expansion of its project pipeline.
Having regard to the nature of the Company's business, these 
transactions are repetitive and continuous in nature and 
are undertaken from time to time depending upon business 
requirements, project execution schedules, commercial 
opportunities, operational exigencies and working capital 
and funding requirements. It is not practical to seek separate 
shareholders' approval for each individual transaction as and 
when the need arises. Accordingly, approval of the Members is 
being sought to enable the Company to enter into such related 
party transactions, contracts, arrangements and agreements 
during the approval period within the maximum limits specified 
in the explanatory statement. The proposed limits are enabling in 
nature and are intended to provide adequate operational flexibility 
to meet business requirements. The actual value of transactions 
undertaken may vary depending upon business needs and may 
be lower than the approved limits. 
The proposed related party transactions of the Company are 
intended to be undertaken in the ordinary course of business and 
on an arm's length basis in accordance with applicable laws and 
the Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions. The pricing 
and commercial terms of such transactions are determined using 
appropriate benchmarking mechanisms, including prevailing 
market prices, comparable third-party quotations, cost-plus 
arrangements, negotiated commercial terms and other generally 
accepted pricing methodologies, having regard to the nature of 
the transaction.
The related party transactions proposed to be entered into by the 
Company are subject to prior approval and periodic review by 
the Audit Committee in accordance with applicable laws and the 
Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions. The related party 
transactions proposed to be entered into with the subsidiaries of 
the Company and other related parties, as set out in this Notice, 
shall also be subject to such approvals as may be required under applicable laws and the respective policies and governance 
framework of the parties concerned, wherever applicable.
Pursuant to Regulation 23 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("Listing Regulations"), 
material related party transactions and subsequent material 
modifications thereto require prior approval of the shareholders 
of the listed entity by way of an ordinary resolution. 
As the annual consolidated turnover of the Company, based on its 
last audited consolidated financial statements for FY 2025-26, is 
H 4,397.12 Crore, the Company falls within the first slab prescribed 
under Schedule XII of the Listing Regulations, applicable to listed 
entities having an annual consolidated turnover of upto H 20,000 
Crore. Accordingly, a related party transaction shall be regarded 
as material if the value of the transaction, whether entered into 
individually or taken together with previous transactions during a 
financial year, exceeds 10% of the Company's annual consolidated 
turnover, being H 439.71 Crore.
Considering the nature and scale of the Company's business 
operations, certain of the proposed related party transactions, 
individually or when aggregated with previous transactions 
undertaken during a financial year with the relevant related 
party(ies), may exceed the applicable materiality threshold during 
the period commencing from the conclusion of this Annual 
General Meeting (AGM) until the conclusion of the next AGM of the 
Company. Accordingly, approval of the Members is being sought 
for the proposed material related party transactions.
The Audit Committee and the Board of Directors, at their 
respective meetings held on 7th August, 2026, have reviewed the 
proposed enabling limits and the nature of the proposed related 
party transactions and, inter alia, considered the commercial 
rationale, business requirements, pricing framework, arm's length 
principles, ordinary course of business criteria and the interests 
of the Company and its minority shareholders. In determining the 
proposed enabling limits, due consideration has been given to the 
Company's expected business growth, expansion of operations, 
anticipated project pipeline, treasury and funding requirements, 
possible inter-group operational arrangements, working capital 
requirements, contingent obligations and business opportunities 
that may arise during the approval period. The proposed limits 
are enabling in nature and are intended to provide the Company 
with adequate operational and financial flexibility to undertake 
transactions as and when business requirements arise. The 
actual value of transactions may be substantially lower than 
the approved limits, and the approval of such enabling limits 
should not be construed as an indication that the entire limits will 
necessarily be utilised during the approval period.
The Audit Committee has also considered the certificate submitted 
by the Chief Financial Officer and the Whole-time Directors of 
the Company in accordance with the Industry Standards on 
"Minimum information to be provided to the Audit Committee and 
Shareholders for approval of Related Party Transactions".
The Audit Committee and the Board of Directors are of the opinion 
that the proposed enabling limits are commercially justified, 
operationally necessary and in the best interests of the Company 
and its shareholders and are not prejudicial to the interests of its 
minority shareholders.

23. Internal Financial Controls
 The Company has in place adequate internal financial controls 
commensurate with the size and nature of its operations. The 
internal financial control framework comprises well-defined 
policies, processes, and procedures designed to ensure 
the orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including 
adherence to company policies, safeguarding of assets, 
prevention and detection of frauds and errors, accuracy and 
completeness of accounting records, and timely preparation 
of reliable financial information.
 These controls are periodically reviewed and tested by the 
internal audit function, and the Audit Committee monitors 
their adequacy and effectiveness. 
 During the year, no material weakness in the design or

2025-26 to Financial Year 2029-30. They have confirmed 
that they are not disqualified from continuing as Secretarial 
Auditors of the Company.
 Pursuant to the provisions of Section 204 of the Companies 
Act, 2013 and the Rules made thereunder, the Secretarial Audit 
Report issued by M/s. J.K. Gupta & Associates, Practising 
Company Secretaries, in Form MR-3 for the Financial Year 
2025-26 is annexed to this Report as Annexure B.
 The Secretarial Auditor has reported observations regarding:
 (a) non-compliance with Rule 3 of the Companies 
(Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 
2014 and Regulation 17(1) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 due 
to the vacancy in the position of Independent Woman 
Director during the period from 21 October 2024 to 5 
April 2025; and
 (b) non-compliance with Regulation 17(1A) of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 in relation to the appointment of an 
Independent Director who had attained the age of 
seventy-five years without obtaining prior approval of 
the shareholders by way of a Special Resolution.
 Board's Explanation:
 The aforesaid observations relate to temporary non-
compliances concerning the composition of the Board. The 
vacancy in the position of Independent Woman Director 
arose during the year and remained unfilled for a limited 
period pending the identification and appointment of a 
suitable candidate. Further, the appointment of Ms. Urvashi 
Saxena as an Independent Director after attaining the age of 
seventy-five years was made prior to obtaining the approval 
of the shareholders by way of a Special Resolution as 
required under Regulation 17(1A) of the Listing Regulations.
 The Company subsequently took the necessary corrective 
measures and achieved compliance with the applicable 
provisions during the Financial Year 2025-26. The Board 
has reviewed the circumstances leading to the aforesaid 
non-compliances and has strengthened its governance 
and compliance monitoring mechanisms to ensure 
timely compliance with all applicable statutory and 
regulatory requirements. 
 Further, in compliance of Regulation 24A of the Listing 
Regulations, the Secretarial Audit Report of the Company’s 
unlisted material subsidiary, Inox Renewable Solutions 
Limited (formerly known as Resco Global Wind Services 
Private Limited) for the Financial Year 2025-26 is annexed to 
this report as Annexure C.28. Reporting of frauds by Auditors 
 During the year, no instance of fraud was reported by

(A) Conservation of Energy
(i) Steps taken or impact on conservation of energy
 As a leading manufacturer of Wind Turbine Generators 
(WTGs) and a fully integrated player in the renewable 
energy sector, the Company continues to focus on resource 
efficiency, sustainable manufacturing practices and 
optimization of energy consumption across its operations.
 Blade Division
 Energy and Resource Optimization
	 Through technology development, process 
improvements, testing and product approvals, the 
Company achieved significant reductions in the 
consumption of energy-intensive materials. During the 
year, savings of approximately H 248 Lakhs in aiding 
materials, H 245 Lakhs in epoxy paste resin and paste 
hardeners and H 25 Lakhs in infusion resin and hardener 
were realized through process optimization initiatives.
	 Optimization of infusion processes and reduction in 
material consumption at critical production stages 
contributed to improved resource utilization, enhanced 
manufacturing efficiency and lower production costs.
 Waste Management and Circular Economy Initiatives
	 Approximately 70 tonnes of process scrap was 
co-processed as an alternative fuel in cement 
manufacturing, thereby reducing landfill disposal and 
supporting resource recovery.
	 Around 182 tonnes of non-grindable process waste 
was co-processed through approved channels for 
environmentally sound disposal.
	 Approximately 500 tonnes of glass fabric and trimming 
waste was recycled for value-added applications.
	 About 170 tonnes of other non-grindable and non-
incinerable waste was diverted for recycling and reuse 
in downstream applications.
 Water Conservation (Mission Pani)
	 Treated wastewater generated from filtration systems 
was reused for utility purposes such as cleaning, 
sanitation and gardening.
	 Sewage water was treated through the Sewage 
Treatment Plant (STP) and reused for horticultural 
purposes within the plant premises.
	 Water consumption in manufacturing processes was 
reduced through the adoption of near zero-water Annexure E 
Information as required under Section 134(3)(m) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with 
Rule 8 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
manufacturing practices, including the replacement of 
water-based processes with alternative technologies.
 Other Energy Efficiency and Resource Optimization 
Measures
	 In-house fabrication of steel platforms, transportation 
supports, structures and modifications resulted in 
savings of approximately H 75 Lakhs and reduced 
dependence on external resources.
	 Replacement of conventional halogen, roof and flood 
lights with energy-efficient LED lighting resulted in 
annual savings of approximately H 40 Lakhs and 
reduced electricity consumption.
 Tower Division
	 Automatic cyclic timers were installed for shop-floor 
lighting to eliminate avoidable energy consumption 
during daytime operations.
	 Process improvements were implemented to optimize 
the consumption of oxygen and other industrial gases.
	 A water treatment facility was commissioned to 
facilitate reuse of treated wastewater for gardening 
and other utility purposes, thereby reducing fresh 
water consumption.
	 High-energy-consuming lighting fixtures were replaced 
with LED-based systems to improve energy efficiency.
 Renewable Energy Commitment
	 The Company remains committed to advancing 
sustainable energy solutions through the design, 
manufacture and supply of Wind Turbine Generators, 
which contribute to reducing dependence on 
conventional fossil fuel-based energy sources.
	 Continuous efforts are undertaken to improve 
operational efficiency, optimize resource utilization 
and enhance environmental performance across 
manufacturing facilities.
(ii) Steps taken by the Company for utilizing alternate 
sources of energy
 The Company operates in the renewable energy sector and 
contributes to the promotion of clean energy through the 
manufacture and supply of Wind Turbine Generators. The 
Company's products facilitate the generation of electricity 
from wind energy and support the transition towards 
sustainable and non-fossil fuel-based energy sources.

1. BRIEF STATEMENT ON THE COMPANY’S 
PHILOSOPHY ON CODE OF GOVERNANCE
 The Company is committed to maintaining the highest 
standards of corporate governance, founded on the 
principles of transparency, integrity, accountability, 
sustainability and ethical business conduct. The Company's 
governance framework supports effective decision-making, 
risk oversight, regulatory compliance and long-term value 
creation for shareholders and other stakeholders. The

and regulatory developments to further strengthen the 
Company's governance architecture.
